text:
jmiller: kicking off a new playback run of last week's production traces with the updated harness. main goals: check determinism after kernel selector changes, validate KV cache warmup behavior, and make sure sampling/anonymization didn't skew perf numbers
ashwin: thanks — can you paste the exact command you used? want to reproduce locally
jmiller: sure: `./playback --trace=/gcs/prod/traces/2026-03-10.tgz --sampler=prob-0.02 --anonymize=pii-scrub --kernels=auto --batch-policy=latency`
rachel: quick note: the `kernels=auto` path changed two weeks ago (switches to fused-attn for short seqs). that could explain small throughput diffs we saw in nightly runs :thinking_face:
jmiller: yeah saw ~6% token/sec drop on the fused path for some traces. need to confirm it's kernel selection and not a batching effect
kc: when you say nondeterminism, is it output tokens or timing metrics?
jmiller: both. outputs are bit-identical after anonymization (good) but trace-level latency distribution shifts between runs. KV cache warmup looks inconsistent when replaying partial sessions — some sessions get cold-kv more often
perf-bot: profiler artifacts uploaded: https://gcs.redwood-inference/profiler/1825123456/ (cpu flame + nvprof) :rocket:
ashwin: can you run with `--kernels=baseline` and `--kernels=fused` and compare? also add `--seed=42` to the harness to force randomized ops order where applicable
jmiller: good idea. added `--seed=42` and two runs: baseline vs fused. attaching quick diff of p50/p95: `baseline: p50=48ms p95=210ms`, `fused: p50=52ms p95=240ms`
rachel: p95 jump is worrying. look at KV cache hit rates per-session. if fused increases per-token compute, batching might be lower SLO and we see more cold cache hits because requests spend longer in-flight
kc: also check the batching heuristic: does the harness simulate real arrival times? synthetic bursts can change selected batch size and affect kernel path
jmiller: harness uses original request timestamps from traces, but we apply a sampler that drops 98% of sessions. that thinning could change inter-arrival distribution. i tried a stratified sampler to preserve burstiness and p95 improved ~3%
ashwin: note for apples-to-apples: lock down `--batch-max-size`, `--timeout-ms`, and `--kv-warmup=true` when comparing kernels. otherwise heuristics will steer differently and you'll be measuring config effects not kernel perf
perf-bot: replay run summary: runA(seed=42,kernels=baseline): tokens=1.2M, kv_hit=0.82, p50=48ms, p95=210ms; runB(seed=42,kernels=fused): tokens=1.2M, kv_hit=0.78, p50=52ms, p95=240ms
jmiller: interesting — tokens identical which suggests sampler deterministic with seed, but kv_hit delta persists. i captured per-session KV hit logs and here's an example snippet:
```
session: s-7392, first_req=0, kv_hits=[0,1,1,1,1], kernel=fused, batch_size=[1,2,4,8], latency_ms=[120,40,35,30]
session: s-4021, first_req=0, kv_hits=[0,0,1,1], kernel=baseline, batch_size=[1,1,2,4], latency_ms=[240,200,60,50]
```
ashwin: that snippet shows fused path has more aggressive batching (good) but first request latency higher — maybe kernel startup cost or memory allocation path. check GPU kernel launch time in nvprof traces
rachel: also run a pure synthetic microbench: same batch sizes and identical token distribution, then compare ci numbers. if fused still slower on microbench, kernel change is suspect. if microbench matches, it's harness/arrival distribution interaction
jmiller: running microbench now with `--synthetic=uniform-10tokens --fixed-arrival=25ms` and will post results
perf-bot: microbench results posted: https://gcs.redwood-inference/micro/1825123456/ — quick summary: fused micro p50=46ms vs baseline p50=45ms, p95 similar. suggests kernel itself isn't dramatically worse in isolation
ashwin: that points back to orchestration: batching heuristics + sampler shaping + KV warmup. for parity tests we should: 1) fix seeds 2) run stratified sampling to preserve burst patterns 3) freeze batching config 4) compare per-session KV hit trajectories 5) check kernel-launch incl. warm caches
kc: i'd add: run a canary against a tiny subset of production in Dedicated (identical HW) to rule out infra differences (driver/kernel versions)
jmiller: noted. i'll run stratified sampler and freeze batching params next. will also diff driver versions across hosts. thanks for eyeballs — ping if you want access to the raw logs
rachel: async: if you need help automating the apples-to-apples matrix, I can add a job to eng-runtime CI that runs baseline vs candidate across the defined knob grid
jmiller: please do — that will speed triage. cc @perf-bot to create a ticket
perf-bot: ticket created: INF-4321 — playback determinism + kernel selection parity checks :white_check_mark:
ashwin: perfect. tentative next steps documented in ticket. :]
